questions.q: What does David ask Yahweh to become for him?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to be his rocky summit of refuge and a stronghold to save him.

questions.q: In whom does David take refuge?
questions.a: David takes refuge in Yahweh.

questions.q: Why does Yahweh lead and guide David?
questions.a: Yahweh leads and guides David for the sake of his own name.

questions.q: What does David believe that Yahweh will protect him from?
questions.a: Yahweh will rescue him from the evil plans his enemies have made to hurt him.

questions.q: Into what does David commit his spirit?
questions.a: David puts himself into the care of Yahweh.

questions.q: Who does David hate?
questions.a: He hates those who keep idols of worthlessness.

questions.q: Why will David be glad and rejoice in Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness?
questions.a: David will be glad and rejoice because Yahweh has seen his affliction and known the troubles of his soul.

questions.q: Where has Yahweh set David’s feet?
questions.a: Yahweh has set David’s feet in an open space.

questions.q: Why does David ask Yahweh to be gracious to him?
questions.a: David is in distress and his eye has wasted away from grief.

questions.q: Why does David’s strength fail and his bones waste away?
questions.a: His strength fails and his bones waste away because of his iniquity.

questions.q: How do people respond to David?
questions.a: His enemies treat him with contempt, his neighbors are especially horrified by him, and those who see him outside flee from him.

questions.q: To what does David compare himself?
questions.a: David says he is as forgotten as a dead man whom no one thinks about, and that he is like a broken vessel.

questions.q: Why is David so troubled?
questions.a: He hears the whispering of many and there is terror on every side, as his enemies conspire together to take his life.

questions.q: From whom does David ask God to rescue him?
questions.a: He asks God to rescue him from his enemies and from those who pursue him.

questions.q: What does David ask God to do for his servant?
questions.a: David asks God to make his face shine upon his servant and to save him in Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness.

questions.q: What does David ask God not to let happen to him?
questions.a: David asks Yahweh not to let him have shame.

questions.q: Why should lying lips be silenced?
questions.a: They speak arrogant and contemptuous things against the righteous.

questions.q: For whom is God’s goodness stored up?
questions.a: Yahweh’s goodness is stored up for those who fear him.

questions.q: From what does Yahweh protect those who revere him?
questions.a: He protects them from the evil plots of the enemies who accuse them.

questions.q: Why is Yahweh to be blessed?
questions.a: Yahweh showed David his marvelous covenant faithfulness when David was in a besieged city.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for David even though David said that he was cut off from God’s eyes?
questions.a: Yahweh heard his plea for help when David cried out to him.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do for his faithful followers?
questions.a: Yahweh preserves the faithful but pays back the proud in full.

questions.q: What advice does David give to those who wait for Yahweh?
questions.a: He tells them to be firm and courageous.

commentary.text: Verses 1–8 Faith and prayer must go together, for the prayer of faith is the prevailing prayer. David gave up his soul in a special manner to God. And with the words, ver. 5, our Lord Jesus yielded up his last breath on the cross, and made his soul a free-will offering for sin, laying down his life as a ransom. But David is here as a man in distress and trouble. And his great care is about his soul, his spirit, his better part. Many think that while perplexed about their worldly affairs, and their cares multiply, they may be excused if they neglect their souls; but we are the more concerned to look to our souls, that, though the outward man perish, the inward man may suffer no damage. The redemption of the soul is so precious, that it must have ceased for ever, if Christ had not undertaken it. Having relied on God's mercy, he will be glad and rejoice in it. God looks upon our souls, when we are in trouble, to see whether they are humbled for sin, and made better by the affliction. Every believer will meet with such dangers and deliverances, until he is delivered from death, his last enemy.

David's troubles made him a man of sorrows. Herein he was a type of Christ, who was acquainted with grief. David acknowledged that his afflictions were merited by his own sins, but Christ suffered for ours. David's friends durst not give him any assistance. Let us not think it strange if thus deserted, but make sure of a Friend in heaven who will not fail. God will be sure to order and dispose all for the best, to all those who commit their spirits also into his hand. The time of life is in God's hands, to lengthen or shorten, make bitter or sweet, according to the counsel of his will. The way of man is not in himself, nor in our friend's hands, nor in our enemies' hands, but in God's. In this faith and confidence he prays that the Lord would save him for his mercies's sake, and not for any merit of his own. He prophesies the silencing of those that reproach and speak evil of the people of God. There is a day coming, when the Lord will execute judgment upon them. In the mean time, we should engage ourselves by well-doing, if possible, to silence the ignorance of foolish men.

Instead of yielding to impatience or despondency under our troubles, we should turn our thoughts to the goodness of the Lord towards those who fear and trust in Him. All comes to sinners through the wondrous gift of the only-begotten Son of God, to be the atonement for their sins. Let not any yield to unbelief, or think, under discouraging circumstances, that they are cut off from before the eyes of the Lord, and left to the pride of men. Lord, pardon our complaints and fears; increase our faith, patience, love, and gratitude; teach us to rejoice in tribulation and in hope. The deliverance of Christ, with the destruction of his enemies, ought to strengthen and comfort the hearts of believers under all their afflictions here below, that having suffered courageously with their Master, they may triumphantly enter into his joy and glory.
